facts.statement: Kelmayisaurus was roughly 10 to 12 meters long.
The known fossil remains consist of a complete left lower jaw with teeth and a partial left upper jaw.
facts.quote: It consists of a complete left dentary with teeth and partial left maxilla.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was discovered in the early 1970s in the Lianmuqin Formation, dating to between 140 and 100 million years ago.
facts.quote: The specimen was found during the early 1970s in the Lianmuqin Formation of the Tugulu Group, dating to the Valanginian-Albian stages between 140 and 100 million years ago.

facts.statement: Fossils of Kelmayisaurus were found near Wuerho in the Junggar Basin.
facts.quote: The discovery locality is near Wuerho in the Junggar Basin.

facts.statement: A 2011 redescription classified Kelmayisaurus as a valid genus within the family Carcharodontosauridae.
facts.quote: In 2011, a redescription of the holotype by Stephen L. Brusatte, Roger B.J. Benson and Xing Xu found Kelmayisaurus to be valid genus of Carcharodontosauridae

facts.statement: Kelmayisaurus is distinguished by a deeply inset accessory groove on the side of its lower jaw bone.
facts.quote: Kelmayisaurus is diagnosable by the form and presence of a deeply inset accessory groove on the lateral side of the dentary

facts.statement: Kelmayisaurus petrolicus was a bipedal carnivore, possibly as large as Allosaurus.
facts.quote: K. petrolicus era un bípedo carnívoro, posiblemente tan grande como Allosaurus.

facts.statement: A supposed second species, K. "gigantus", was once described as a 22-meter vertebral column that would make it the longest theropod, but this is now considered a nomen nudum and a mistake for a sauropod.
facts.quote: Grady mencionó una supuesta segunda especie, K. "gigantus", en un libro para niños en 1993 como una columna vertebral gigantesca que proviene de un espécimen de 22 metros, lo cual lo convertiría en el terópodo más largo

facts.statement: Kelmayisaurus lived approximately 140 to 100 million years ago.
facts.quote: hace aproximadamente 140 a 100 millones de años

facts.statement: The time range for Kelmayisaurus is from the Valanginian to the Albian stages, between 137.05 and 100.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Valanginian to Albian (137.05 to 100.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: A 2026 study reported an isolated theropod tooth from the Lianmuqin Formation suggesting the presence of a medium-sized tetanuran alongside Kelmayisaurus petrolicus and small coelurosaurs.
facts.quote: Li et al. (2026) report the discovery of an isolated theropod tooth from the Lower Cretaceous Lianmuqin Formation (China), interpreted as evidence indicating that, in addition to Kelmayisaurus petrolicus and small coelurosaurs, the theropod assemblage from the studied formation also included a medium-sized tetanuran.

rejected.statement: Kelmayisaurus is an extinct genus of carcharodontosaurian theropod dinosaur that lived during the Early Cretaceous.
rejected.quote: Kelmayisaurus (meaning "Karamay lizard") is an extinct genus of carcharodontosaurian theropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous.

rejected.statement: Kelmayisaurus was first named and described by Chinese paleontologist Dong Zhiming in 1973.
rejected.quote: It was first named and described by Chinese paleontologist Dong Zhiming in 1973
